A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MULTITP study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; v6 retains Appendices A–E and adds Appendix F.

before.justification: V5 reports original evaluations of 19 LLMs, translation-quality assessments, and multilingual and robustness analyses in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V6 retains those empirical results and adds original comparisons of four uncensored model variants with their original counterparts in Section 6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Beyond the retained token-forcing setup, v6 applies an uncensoring intervention attributed to Arditi et al. to four models. This adds a limited procedure for reducing refusals; the core scenario-generation and preference-assessment methods remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same multilingual trolley-problem task, 107-language coverage, six moral dimensions, and translation-evaluation coverage. The revised vignette counts do not establish additional languages, populations, or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 2a adds uncensored counterparts of Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 2B It (labeled Gemma 2 2B in the figures), Qwen 2 7B, and Llama 2 7B. Appendix F compares each with its original counterpart; the original 19-model comparison set is retained.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 and Table 2 revise the reported vignette count from 920 to 460 per language and the total from 97,520 to 98,440. These are reported count revisions, without establishing data regeneration or reruns. Section 6 also adds original-versus-uncensored comparisons for four selected models.

E4.justification: V5 proposes advanced refusal mitigation as future work; v6 adds a focused four-model analysis of whether uncensoring changes moral preferences and refusal rates across the six dimensions (Figures 12–15). Existing paraphrase, option-order, translation, and regional analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The fixed-seed statement, existing significance reporting, and translation-score variability reporting are unchanged. The new uncensoring results introduce no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 2a adds results placing uncensored Qwen 2 7B and Llama 3.1 8B ahead of the original leading model, Llama 3.1 70B. Figures 12–15 add preference and refusal-rate results, with the largest refusal reductions shown for Llama 3.1 8B. These are new variant results, not revised scores for the original models; Table 2 also changes the reported dataset counts.

T1.justification: The preference-vector definitions, L2 misalignment metric, language aggregation, and language-sensitivity formulation are unchanged. V6 adds no formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about MULTITP, multilingual moral alignment, widespread model–human misalignment, and the absence of a strong high-resource-language advantage. The count corrections and additional experiment do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 now interprets the uncensoring experiments as improving measured human alignment and reducing refusals, while acknowledging that refusals persist. Appendix F additionally identifies stronger effectiveness for Llama 3.1 8B. Existing qualifications about descriptive human preferences, trolley-problem scope, and language-to-country mapping remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Existing model identifiers, decoding settings, resource and cost information, prompt templates, and code/data access information remain unchanged. The new uncensoring study cites its methodological source but supplies no additional implementation settings, modified-model identifiers, or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: V6 adds Arditi et al., Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction, as the source of its uncensoring intervention. The existing related-work discussion and broader positioning of MULTITP are unchanged.

P1.justification: The jailbreaking future-work paragraph becomes a dedicated Section 6 with experimental discussion; Future Work and Conclusion are renumbered, and Appendix F and acknowledgments are added. Headers change from Preprint 2024 to the ICLR 2025 publication statement. Most existing prose and organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2a is redrawn to include four additional model variants, and Figures 12–15 introduce paired preference/refusal radar plots. Other figures and table structures are retained apart from small placement adjustments. Figure 2a's caption still describes 19 models despite displaying the added variants.

improvement.justification: V6 turns v5's proposed refusal-mitigation direction into empirical comparisons, providing useful evidence about the sensitivity of measured alignment to uncensoring. This partially addresses an acknowledged evaluation weakness. The gain is limited by sparse implementation details, persistent refusals, unexplained vignette-count revisions, and Figure 2's incompletely updated caption and accompanying results text.
